citation: Millington, J., Romero-Calcerrada, R., Wainwright, J. and Perry, G. (2008). An Agent-Based Model of Mediterranean Agricultural Land-Use/Cover Change for Examining Wildfire Risk. JASSS 11(4) 4.

dedupe_keys.name: agent based model of mediterranean agricultural land use cover change for wildfire risk

description: This agent-based model simulates agricultural land-use and land-cover change in a Mediterranean landscape to examine how farmer decisions change wildfire risk. Two farmer types make decisions: commercial agents that act on economic returns and traditional agents driven by cultural motives, and their choices on land tenure units shape the mosaic of crops, pasture and shrubland that fuels fire. It was built by James Millington, Raúl Romero-Calcerrada, John Wainwright and George Perry and published in 2008 in the Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation (JASSS). The case area is the protected area SPA 56 'Encinares del río Alberche y Cofio' in central Spain, starting from the 1999 landscape. The model was written in NetLogo and recoded in C++, and both versions are available from a link in the free open-access article; the code licence is not stated. Caveats: it is calibrated to one landscape and dates from 2008, and the external code link may not persist. The study found that land tenure structure strongly shapes land-use trajectories and that mean wildfire risk rises relative to 1999. For simulation it shows how to couple farmer agents with hazard exposure, useful for wildfire risk studies near rural infrastructure. It is related to the CoMSES Net Computational Model Library record in this catalogue, which hosts comparable land-use models.
